thread:
maya: heads up — console preview for header-routing rules is now in canary and we saw weird quota attributions from a subset of mobile clients :grimacing:

arjun: ugh what does "weird" mean here?

maya: some requests that should be matched by `X-Redwood-Route` are landing on the default route and getting charged to tenant A instead of the proxy tenant. repro rate ~0.6% of mobile traffic.

leo: is it UA parsing/normalization? mobile SDKs send a lot of garbage UAs.

maya: partially. two things collided: 1) console preview adds a transient header `X-RW-Preview: <id>` for route resolution, 2) our legacy mobile proxy rewrites UA and strips unknown headers in certain cases. result: preview header absent -> gateway falls back to `User-Agent` heuristics -> misroute.

anya: can you paste the example headers from a failing request?

maya: sure — minimal snippet:

```
X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4
User-Agent: RedwoodMobile/1.2.3 (Android) /custom-proxy
Authorization: Bearer ephemeral-xxx
```

Note proxy removes `X-RW-Preview` 100% of the time when it sees `/custom-proxy` in UA.

samir: so the preview header never reaches the gateway in these flows. Then our route matcher looks at UA and tries to apply legacy tenant heuristics.

arjun: what's the quota implication? are tokens billed to wrong tenant or to default?

maya: billed to default then reconciled later in batch, but realtime per-route quotas and throttles fire incorrectly. customers hit rate limits even though their commit is fine.

leo: hmm telemetry is also skewed — dashboard shows spikes on default route. ops alerts went off.

anya: proposal A — make console preview use signed header `X-RW-Preview-Sig` that proxies can't strip without breaking signature. downside: rollout complexity + key management.

arjun: proposal B — make route matching prefer explicit `X-Redwood-Route` over UA regardless of preview, and make preview header an additive hint only for console UI. That way even if preview is missing, we still require explicit route header to override.

samir: we already prioritize `X-Redwood-Route`, but in this case the proxy removed both preview and route headers. it's only UA left.

maya: correct. fallback to UA is the problem. we could change fallback behavior to only match UA when the request has a verified auth context (signed JWT with tenant claim). if no auth, treat as unverified and route to a safe default that doesn't charge tenant.

leo: that would protect quota but may be surprising for some flows. also many mobile clients use ephemeral tokens without tenant claim.

anya: could we instead emit a telemetry tag `routing.eval=ua-fallback` so console clearly surfaces when UA heuristics were used? then ops can filter dashboards and exclude those from quota reconciliation.

arjun: I like the telemetry tag + temporary conservative routing (send to isolated "unverified" bucket) for 2 weeks while we evaluate. lowers blast radius.

samir: +1. also add an alert suppression rule: if many accounts move from tenant -> default due to ua-fallback, don't page on the first 5m incidence.

maya: plan:
- short term (canary): add `routing.eval=ua-fallback` telemetry and route to `unverified` bucket when preview/header missing and auth claim absent.
- mid term: console preview switches to signed preview header and we publish key rotation doc.
- long term: SDKs + proxies updated to preserve preview/route headers or surface them to the gateway via `X-Forwarded-Client-Headers` mapping.

anya: what's the impact on quota dashboards? we should mark affected time windows and surface reconciliation notes.

leo: will add a Dashboard annotation generator that tags ranges where `routing.eval=ua-fallback` > 0.1% of requests.

maya: I've created a canary flag `console.header-preview-safe-route` on the gateway. enabling for 10% of traffic now. logs and telemetry hooked.

deploy-bot: deploy start: gateway/service v6.12.3 -> canary cluster (10%) by maya.

samir: I'll monitor rate limit alerts and quota billing logs. will report back in 20m.

maya: thanks — if we see anything worse, rollback the flag.

arjun: follow-up: we should document this in the console rollout checklist and add a checkbox: "ensure proxies forward X-RW-* headers".

maya: added to the checklist and PR coming to docs. :white_check_mark:

console-bot: note: UI preview will show "Routing heuristics applied (UA fallback)" when the telemetry tag is present.

leo: great. good mitigation path.

samir: update: initial 20m look — ua-fallback spikes correlate exactly with proxy UA marker. telemetry tag appears as expected. no additional rate-limit pages so far.

maya: excellent. filing follow-up ticket to track signed-preview work and SDK changes.

arjun: thanks everyone. we'll regroup tomorrow during standup to decide canary expansion. :thumbsup:
